context:
Land this only after break-root-import-cycle and
relocate-cli-hook-registries merge, so the layers contract can start
clean (or near-clean) instead of needing a large allowlist from day one.
Start every contract in permissive/allowlisted form (w2, w3), verify it
passes on current `develop`, then wire it into CI (w4) so it locks in the
current state rather than blocking on a large simultaneous cleanup.
Ratchet the allowlist down in follow-up PRs as remove-or-integrate-legacy-

description:
Architecture review (Work Area E, structural remediation) found no import
layering/architecture-boundary enforcement tooling exists anywhere in the
repo: no `import-linter`, no `tach`, no equivalent config in
`pyproject.toml`, `Makefile`, or `.github/workflows/*.yml` (confirmed by
search - zero hits). The intended layering is currently only a convention:
`utils < core < platforms < cli` (lower layers must not import higher
layers), with `benchbox.experimental` and `benchbox.mcp` expected to stay
isolated (not imported by the core dependency chain). Nothing today
detects a violation of that convention before it ships, which is how the
inversions fixed by `break-root-import-cycle` and
`relocate-cli-hook-registries` were able to accumulate unnoticed.

This TODO adds `import-linter` with contracts encoding that layering, run
in CI, so future violations fail fast instead of silently growing into
another SCC or layering inversion.

Known existing violation to handle explicitly rather than ignore:
`benchbox/platforms/cudf.py:16` imports `benchbox.experimental.gpu` at
module top level, which breaks an `experimental isolated` contract. The
planning entry `remove-or-integrate-legacy-cudf-platform-module.yaml`
already owns deciding whether that module is removed, quarantined, or
integrated - do not duplicate that decision here; this TODO either (a)
allowlists the violation as a named exception until that TODO resolves it,
or (b) is sequenced after it if it lands first. See deps.needs.

This is a tooling/enforcement addition, not a shrink-campaign item -
`_project/goal-shrink-core-code.md` scopes structural/architecture work
like this out of the autonomous shrink loop.

anti_patterns.dont: duplicate the cudf.py experimental-import decision here
anti_patterns.why: remove-or-integrate-legacy-cudf-platform-module owns it; just reference it as the allowlist's resolution path.

anti_patterns.dont: invent a new CI job for this
anti_patterns.why: extend the existing lint job pattern (make lint-markers -> pr.yml) rather than adding a separate workflow.

anti_patterns.dont: write contracts with zero exceptions before verifying they pass
anti_patterns.why: lint-imports failing on day one blocks unrelated PRs; start allowlisted, ratchet down.

preserves.behavior: The contract does not require moving any code beyond what break-root-import-cycle, relocate-cli-hook-registries, and remove-or-integrate-legacy-cudf-platform-module already do - this TODO adds detection, not further remediation.
make lint and the pr.yml lint job continue to pass for all currently-green code once residual known violations are explicitly allowlisted.

prior_art.concept: Makefile:lint-markers target and .github/workflows/pr.yml:288 ('Validate test marker annotations' step calling make lint-markers) - the existing pattern of a narrow, purpose-built Makefile lint target wired into the pr.yml lint job; extend this pattern for import-linter rather than inventing a new CI-wiring convention.

remove-or-integrate-legacy-cudf-platform-module.yaml - owns the decision on benchbox/platforms/cudf.py's benchbox.experimental.gpu import; this TODO's experimental-isolation contract must reference, not duplicate, that decision.

verifications.description: import-linter runs and reports the configured contracts
verifications.expected: contracts checked; only explicitly allowlisted violations (if any) are reported, no unexpected failures

verifications.description: New CI step is present and passes in the lint job
verifications.expected: import-linter step runs as part of make lint with the same pass/fail semantics as lint-markers

work_units.notes:
Added `import-linter>=2.13` to `[dependency-groups].dev` in
pyproject.toml via `uv add --group dev import-linter` (pulls in
`grimp` transitively). Added `.importlinter` (v2.13 uses the classic
INI-style config file, not `[tool.importlinter]` in pyproject.toml)
with `root_package = benchbox` and zero contracts first - confirmed
`uv run -- lint-imports` runs clean (963 files, 2840 dependencies, 0
contracts) before adding any contract.
work_units.summary: Add import-linter dependency and base config

work_units.notes:
Added the `layers` contract. Reality did not match the "few to none
left" expectation: running `lint-imports` with a zero-exception
layers contract surfaced ~46 real current violations (not just the
illustrative cudf/path_utils/format_selection/core-registry examples
cited when this TODO was filed) - see the parent TODO/session report
for the full enumerated list now encoded as named `ignore_imports`
entries in `.importlinter`, grouped into: utils->core (3 modules doing
a lazy `import benchbox` root-import fallback, cascading through
benchbox/__init__.py, plus one direct `path_utils -> core.runtime_paths`
edge), utils->cli (1 direct edge, `config_interface -> cli.config`),
utils->platforms (1 direct edge, `format_selection ->
platforms.base.format_capabilities`), and core->platforms (8 modules
with the same lazy root-import pattern + ~26 direct edges from the
platform-registry/factory/dispatch/equivalence-comparison call sites
in core.dryrun, core.runner.runner, core.platform_registry,
core.tpchavoc.equivalence, core.dataframe.maintenance_interface,
etc). Each entry has a one-line justification comment; none are
loosened via wildcards on the layer/package level. `lint-imports`
is GREEN with these allowlisted.
work_units.summary: Add the layers contract: utils < core < platforms < cli

work_units.notes:
Deviated from the literal `type = "independence"` instruction after
actually running it: independence forces ALL listed modules to be
mutually exclusive in both directions, so listing
core/platforms/cli/utils/experimental together immediately broke on
the legitimate cli->core, platforms->core, core->utils, etc. edges
that the layers contract above explicitly allows (core/platforms/
cli/utils are not independent of each other, only of experimental).
Used `type = "forbidden"` instead (source_modules =
core/platforms/cli/utils, forbidden_modules = experimental), which is
the correct one-directional primitive; kept the single named
allowlist exception for `benchbox/platforms/cudf.py ->
benchbox.experimental.gpu` citing
remove-or-integrate-legacy-cudf-platform-module (still not landed,
confirmed via `grep -rn "experimental" benchbox/platforms/cudf.py`).
For mcp: ran
`grep -rn "benchbox.mcp" benchbox/core benchbox/platforms benchbox/cli benchbox/utils`
(zero hits - nothing in the lower layers imports mcp) and
`grep -rn "^from benchbox\|^import benchbox" benchbox/mcp/**/*.py`
(mcp extensively and legitimately imports core/utils to expose
benchmark data and execution via MCP tools, resolving this TODO's own
open_questions entry). A bidirectional independence contract would
have required re-allowlisting every one of those core/utils imports,
defeating the point, so mcp also uses `type = "forbidden"`
(source_modules = core/platforms/cli/utils, forbidden_modules = mcp)
with zero exceptions needed - it passes cleanly today.
work_units.summary: Add independence/isolation contracts for experimental and mcp

work_units.notes:
Added a standalone `lint-imports:` Makefile target (mirrors the
`lint-markers` pattern exactly - a narrow, separately-invoked target,
not folded into `make lint`) running `uv run -- lint-imports`, added
it to `.PHONY` and the `make help` listing, and added a "Validate
import layering" step calling `make lint-imports` in
`.github/workflows/pr.yml`'s `code-lint` job immediately after the
existing "Validate test marker annotations" (`make lint-markers`)
step (pr.yml:288 area), per the cited prior art. `tests/unit/workflows/`
(21 tests, incl. `test_pr_workflow_path_classifier.py` which parses
pr.yml) still pass unmodified - no pin updates were needed.
work_units.summary: Wire import-linter into make lint and pr.yml
